File > Calendar Colour > a calendar opens a colour sheet of nine named system colours (Green, Orange, Purple, Pink, Teal, Indigo, Blue, Brown, Gray, from overlay::PALETTE; no red, which is the today marker and the destructive colour) with a swatch and a check mark: a tap picks a row, Done (or Return) gives the calendar the colour, Cancel (or Escape) keeps the old one, Up and Down move the pick. features.note: Go > Search Events... (Command-F) and a toolbar button open a search screen with a query field and scrolling result list; Return or a click opens the event. Saved events match on title, location and notes, and from:YYYY-MM-DD and to:YYYY-MM-DD words limit the hits to a date range (search.rs, tested headless in tests/parity_app-calendar.rs). Uses its own list rather than the kit search_field; the caret does not move by click.

features.feature: Drag to create / move events in Day and Week
features.note: Dragging empty hour-grid space sizes a new event (15 minute snap) and opens the editor; dragging a timed event moves it across times and week days and saves; its top or bottom edge resizes it (layout::drag_resize); an all-day event in the band above the hours moves to the day under the pointer (drag.rs Kind::AllDay, saved with the series for a repeating event). With a finger the press must be held 250 ms first, so a press that moves at once scrolls. With a mouse or trackpad the drag starts as soon as the pointer has moved 4 points, with no hold: the app takes touch events and reads the touch type of each touch (main.rs touches, Calendar::set_pointer). The shell makes the wheel as a press followed by a short burst of moves (the Wayland path: press, a move 16 ms later, a lift at 32 ms; the evdev path eases a finger), and an app cannot tell that from a hand, so a move that comes within 30 ms of its press is taken as the wheel and scrolls. Under a view time zone the grid place of a moved or resized block is turned back to the event's own clock before it is saved. Tested headless in calendar/tests.rs. Code only: not built or run, not verified on Midget. Left: the travel time padding is not resized with the edge, and the 30 ms rule is a heuristic until the shell marks the touch a wheel notch makes.
features.wire: Have the shell mark the touch a wheel notch makes (a distinct touch type or contact id) so the 30 ms rule can go. Midget check: in Week view drag a block with the mouse without waiting, scroll with the wheel over a block (it scrolls and the block does not move), drag an all-day event to another day.

features.note: Holidays row in the calendar list shows Iceland's public holidays and observances (Easter computed) as read-only all-day events. The Birthdays row shows the birthdays of the cards in Contacts as read-only all-day items ("Ana Lind's Birthday", with the age in the notes when the card has a year of birth); a 29 February birthday falls on 1 March in a common year. Calendar reads Contacts' own files (appdata/is.olibuijr.contacts.desktop/Contacts/contacts.tsv and details.txt, the way it reads Reminders) when the shown year changes or the row is switched on; it never writes a card, and the names and dates stay on the machine (birthdays.rs, tested headless in tests/parity_app-calendar-w15b.rs). Settings > Default Birthday Alert (none, on the day, 1 or 2 days or a week before, each at 9 AM) plans the alerts with the other events through the alert service and the Up Next list, and the events are never written to calendar.ics. Code only: not built or run, not verified on Midget. Left: a region choice for the holidays, a Contacts service query instead of reading its files, and the Birthdays row does not refresh while the file changes. Midget check: add a birthday to a card in Contacts, switch Birthdays on in Calendar, open that day.
features.wire: Add a region choice for the holidays, and read the birthdays through a Contacts service query when the shell has one.

features.apple: PreferencesPanel.nib time zone support; TimeZonePickerSheet.nib; InspectorTimeZoneView.nib
features.note: A Time Zone row in the event form cycles the device's zone, UTC, Iceland and nine more zones with their daylight saving rules (calendar/zones.rs: London, Paris, Helsinki, New York, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, India, Tokyo; the European and North American shift rules, tested at the shift days). The zone sets the alarms per occurrence, so a repeating event in a zone with summer time fires at the right moment on both sides of the shift (alerts.rs utc_offset_secs), and is written as TZID in the .ics export with a STANDARD and DAYLIGHT block with yearly rules (ics.rs write, zones::vtimezone_body). The toolbar's Time Zone button steps through the zones and back to each event's own time, and View > Time Zone chooses one: the Day and Week grids, the month cells, the agenda and the printed grid then show each timed event where it falls on that zone's clock (viewzone.rs, zones::convert_clock; all-day events keep their day), and a block moved or resized in the grid is saved on the event's own clock. The choice is kept in calendar-prefs.txt. Code only: not built or run, not verified on Midget. Left: southern-hemisphere zones, reading the rules of an imported VTIMEZONE (an imported zone not in the table keeps the fixed offset its file gives), and the Day and Week views do not say which zone they show beyond the button's name. Midget check: `cargo test -p bifrost-calendar zones viewzone alerts` pass; then give an event the Tokyo zone, press the toolbar Time Zone button until it reads New York: the event is on the day before; File > Export Calendar holds a DAYLIGHT block with an RRULE for a Paris event.
features.wire: Show the view zone's name in the Day and Week headers; add the southern-hemisphere zones.

features.note: A list of an imported event's attendees. When the account organises a saved event that has invitees, the saved event goes to them as an iTIP REQUEST (METHOD:REQUEST, the event's own lines, written to itip-requests/) by Mail, on Save (rsvp.rs invite_attendees). The event form's Add Invitees row opens a line: type an email address, or the first letters of a name and the people of the address book Contacts keeps with an address show under the line (up to three, birthdays.rs book and suggest; nothing is looked up anywhere else). Return adds the address, or the first match; a tap on a match adds that person with their name; each invitee has a Remove row; up to 20 per event. The invitees are kept with the event (calendar-extras.txt, invitee lines) and saving the event writes a METHOD:REQUEST for them (organiser the account's address, the repeat rule and the zone included) into itip-requests/ and opens it in Mail, which sends it (inviting.rs invite_new_attendees); without an account address the invitees are kept and the notice says no invitation was sent. Tested headless in calendar/tests.rs. Code only: not built or run, not verified on Midget. Left: sending through CalDAV scheduling (a PUT to the server), showing the answers of people added here (they show only in the reply mail), and a role for each invitee. Midget check: new event, Add Invitees, type the first letters of a contact, tap the match, Save: Mail opens with the invitation attached.
features.wire: Send through CalDAV scheduling when the server advertises it (no scheduling PUT exists yet).

features.feature: Respond to invitations; show declined events
features.apple: View > Show Declined Events; notifications settings
features.bifrost: springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/src/calendar/rsvp.rs:94 (respond: PARTSTAT update); springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/src/calendar/rsvp.rs:75 (reply_text: METHOD:REPLY); springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/src/calendar/rsvp.rs:136 (respond_to_invitation: saves calendar.ics and the reply); springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/src/calendar/ics.rs:407 (ORGANIZER parse); springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/src/calendar/overlay.rs:111 (sync_declined, hides declined events); springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/src/calendar.rs:1571 (Accept, Maybe, Decline rows)
features.note: In the event editor, Accept, Maybe and Decline show when the account address (the CalDAV account username, rsvp.rs:174) is an invitee with PARTSTAT=NEEDS-ACTION. The answer is written to calendar.ics, and an iTIP REPLY (METHOD:REPLY, one ATTENDEE line, RFC 5546) is saved to itip-replies/. The reply then opens in Mail (mail_compose), addressed to the organiser with that .ics attached; the person sends it from Mail. View > Show Declined Events (off by default) shows the events the account declined. Tests in calendar/rsvp.rs cover the PARTSTAT parse, the exact reply text, the answer, the mail message and the declined filter; not built or run, and nothing is verified on Midget.
features.wire: Accept, Maybe and Decline are editor rows, not a popover, and are not in the accessibility tree. An answered invitation cannot be changed from Calendar yet. The declined set is refreshed when the saved-event count changes, not after an edit. Sending is through Mail only; CalDAV scheduling (PUT to the organiser's inbox) is not used.

features.note: File > Print... (Cmd+P) draws the shown day, week, month or year as a grid on a landscape A4 page (printgrid.rs): the month as a table with each day's events in its cell and "n more" when a cell is full; the week and the day as columns on an hourly grid with a block for each event (overlapping ones side by side, the times and the place inside the block, all-day events in a band above the hours); the year as twelve small months with the days that have events shaded. Two standard fonts (Helvetica and Helvetica-Bold) in WinAnsi, so the letters of Western European languages print (the Icelandic ones included) and other scripts print as ?. A shorter week prints the days it shows; a view time zone moves the events as the grid shows them. The agenda text of the same range is still built (printing.rs print_job). Drawing is pure and tested headless (printgrid.rs, tests/parity_app-calendar-w15b.rs). Code only: not built or run, not verified on Midget. Left: more than one page for a busy range, a print sheet for the paper size, and non-Latin text.
features.wire: Check File > Print... on Midget with Save as PDF and compare the page with the window.
